claim_verdicts.evidence: Curriculum definition of breaking change (outline item 1, glossary breaking-change short_en). Definitional; the listed cases (remove/rename/retype a response field, optional request field made required) follow directly from the definition. No vendor document governs it.

git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs lines 5-9: `public sealed record ProductDto(int Id, string Name, int PriceVnd);` `public sealed record OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd);` `public sealed record OrderDto(int Id, int CustomerId, string Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, List<OrderItemDto> Items);` Code block matches character-for-character.

formatting.md (moniker >= aspnetcore-7.0, line 554): "The following highlighted code configures PascalCase formatting instead of the default camelCase formatting". Program.cs at stage-1 only calls AddControllers() with no JsonOptions override. Execution: curl /api/v1/products/1 -> {"id":1,"name":"Bàn phím cơ","priceVnd":1250000}.

git show stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/models.dart lines 10-14: `factory Product.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => Product(id: json['id'] as int, name: json['name'] as String, priceVnd: json['priceVnd'] as int,);` Code block (lines 3-15) matches character-for-character.

Executed with Dart SDK 3.13.2 (the pinned flutter.dart): map from jsonDecode('{"id":1,"name":"x","price":1250000}'); print(m['priceVnd']) -> `null`; `m['priceVnd'] as int` -> `_TypeError: type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'int' in type cast`. No local Dart language docs in refs/; evidence is execution.
Executed with Dart SDK 3.13.2: jsonDecode('{"priceVnd":"1250000"}')['priceVnd'] as int -> `_TypeError: type 'String' is not a subtype of type 'int' in type cast`.

stage-1:DonHang.App/lib/api_client.dart line 29: `return items.map((item) => Product.fromJson(item as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList();` inside `Future<List<Product>> fetchProducts() async`; an exception thrown during toList() completes the returned Future with that error. product_list_screen.dart then renders `Could not load products: ${snapshot.error}`.

Round 2, rewritten text. stage-1 models.dart: `factory OrderResult.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => OrderResult(id: json['id'] as int, status: json['status'] as String,);` - no other key read. OrdersController.Create returns CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order)) (ActionResult<OrderDto>); captured stage-1 output shows id, customerId, status, placedAt, items.

Executed with Dart SDK 3.13.2: map from jsonDecode('{"id":1,"status":"new","extra":5}'); `t['id'] as int`, `t['status'] as String` -> prints `C 1 new`, no error: an extra key is simply never looked up by a by-name reader.

Conservative working rule mandated by outline item 4, not a vendor behaviour. The premise (the server receives requests only and has no view of client parsing code) is definitional of HTTP client/server; the conclusion is a stated policy, and the lesson frames it as how a change 'counts', not as a documented fact.

Ran `curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products/1` against the running lab: `{"id":1,"name":"Bàn phím cơ","priceVnd":1250000}`. Lab checkout is stage-2, but stage-1 capture outputs/stage-1/scripts/backend/auth-and-orders.txt shows the same object for id 1 in the list, and stage-1 ProductsController.Get returns Ok(new ProductDto(...)); db/seed.sql: (1, 'Bàn phím cơ', 1250000).

issues.quote: If both answers are no, the change only adds.
issues.text: Overstated: two 'no' answers do not imply the change only adds. A change that keeps every name and type and every request working can still alter what a client reads, e.g. sending priceVnd in thousands of dong instead of dong, which fits the Core concepts definition of breaking change. The diagram node D has the same shortcut.
issues.fix: Replace with: "If both answers are no, as when a change only adds a field, nothing a client reads by name and type has gone." Optionally rename node D to "No: safe for a client that reads only known fields".
